axisel.com redesignConcept reviewSeptember 2026

Three ways to rebuild axisel.com around Grow together.

The current site is a generic dark-mode SaaS template wearing an old logo. The new brand guide asks for something warmer, more human, and more specific to Lebanon. Below: what is wrong today, what the guide asks for, three fully immersive concepts with working mockups, and the stack I recommend building on.

Client feedback, 10 September: Concept A, with B's warmth.

The client chose A for the 23.5° geometry and physics, and also responded to B's togetherness and merchant photography. Concept D below blends them, roughly 80 percent A and 20 percent B. The client confirmed D, and the homepage has since been built as a fully animated Astro 7 site: open it from the Concept D section.

01 · Where the site is today

A capable product, presented as a corporate "commerce intelligence layer."

  • Wrong brand

    Old star-burst logo; near-black #0A0A0A instead of Ink Navy; a muted champagne gold instead of Signal Gold; no Ember Coral anywhere; a heavy display serif instead of Instrument Serif. Almost nothing on the page comes from the 2026 guide.

  • Wrong voice

    The guide positions Axisel as accessible and human. The site speaks like an enterprise vendor: "connected commerce intelligence layer," "every pixel optimized by AI to maximize your ROI," "join the region's top brands." The actual audience is a social seller in Achrafieh.

  • Hero is borrowed

    The homepage hero plays a Starbucks UK YouTube ad as background video, complete with "[Music]" captions. Third-party content, off-brand, and a licensing exposure.

  • Loose ends

    "200 templates and counting" on one page, "50 production-ready designs" on another. Leftover "UI · placeholder" text on the Solutions page. Two different Book-a-Demo routes. A footer with 30+ links, most pointing at pages that do not exist yet.

  • Photography

    Generic stock imagery (hangers, makeup flat-lays, headphones) directly contradicts the guide's rule: real merchants, real products, hard light, never stock.

  • Motion

    Lenis smooth scroll and a few fade-ins. Not immersive. Nothing about the movement says "axis," "23.5°," or "grow together."

  • Tech

    Next.js on Vercel, client-rendered. The pricing page renders nothing without JavaScript. Easy to replace: the site is content, not an app.

Worth keeping

  • The pricing structure and the "no commission on your sales" argument. It is the clearest thing on the site.
  • The Why Axisel comparison against a fragmented Shopify/Wix/Woo stack, and its FAQ.
  • The template library idea: 50 storefronts, each studied from a leading brand in its category.
  • The problem framing: "you are not losing momentum because of your products, you are losing it in the system."
02 · What the brand guide asks for

Capable and warm, at the same time.

The 2026 guidelines (PAPA agency) are unusually specific about strategy. The site has to carry all of it, not just the colors.

Purpose

Structure, not more ideas.

Entrepreneurs in Lebanon are not short on ideas, they are short on structure. Axisel gives them the tools, speed, and support to turn ideas into real, sustainable businesses.

Audience

Defined by stage, not age.

From a first-time social seller testing an idea to an established shop owner who has never had a website. They are already doing the work. They need structure without hiring a team or learning to code.

Positioning

Full platform, still human.

Shopify is powerful but technical. Wix is simple but shallow. Axisel claims the empty quadrant: real commerce infrastructure that stays accessible.

Values

  • Speed. Remove the technical work between an idea and a store.
  • Entrepreneurship. Turn skills, products, and social businesses into structured ones.
  • Community. A local network that learns and grows together, online and at events.

Voice

  • Clear, confident, approachable. A knowledgeable partner, not a corporation explaining its technology.
  • Slightly serious, slightly casual, clearly friendly, leaning inspiring.
  • Keywords: approachable, clear, confident, intelligent, helpful, optimistic.

The mark

23.5°, and a gap.

Two planes cut at the Earth's axis tilt, gold running into coral in opposite directions. The gap between them is not a border, it is an opening: the platform as a way in, not a wall. Two sides meeting mid-transaction.

Intelligent, but not complicated.Fast, but not careless. Professional, but not corporate.Young, but not childish. Local, but not limited.Human, but still technologically serious.

Instrument Serif italic for the human words

Instrument Serif for display (104 / 64 / 48 / 37 px), Inter for body and interface (27 / 21 / 16 px), Bricolage Grotesque only in the wordmark. Three patterns, one angle: Axis Hairline (fine 23.5° lines), Dash Rhythm (gold and coral dashes), Window Facet (the icon tessellated, hero moments only). Icons: 1.6 px outline, one accent dot. Photography: hard directional light, tight tilted crops, navy-to-coral grade, real merchants, never stock.

Concept A

On Axis

The 23.5° axis becomes the site's physics. Everything enters, moves, and settles along the mark's tilt. The gap between the two planes is literally the way in: as you scroll, the planes part and the product passes through the opening. Bright bone ground, navy for the deep beats, gold and coral only where the brand puts them.

BrightGeometricKinetic typeClosest to the guideWarm, not dark
Open live mockup ↗

Signature motion

  1. Load: the axis hairline sweeps across, type rises in four beats, the mark floats.
  2. Scroll: the planes separate and content passes through the gap (GSAP ScrollTrigger pin + scrub).
  3. Every reveal travels along 23.5°, then settles level. A tiny tilted plane follows the cursor.
  4. Page changes: the two planes close over the page and open on the next (View Transitions).

Best if

You want the site to feel unmistakably like the new identity, bright and optimistic rather than another dark SaaS page, and you want it to work before a photoshoot exists. It differentiates hardest from Shopify's and Wix's marketing sites.

Watch out for

  • The hero mark should be a real WebGL object (light, gradient, slight parallax) to earn "immersive." Plan one week for it.
  • Tilted UI cards must settle level before anyone needs to read them.
  • Needs discipline: the angle everywhere becomes noise if every element tilts.
Concept B

Grow Together

An editorial, photography-led site about the merchants, not the software. The mark is rebuilt out of two photographs: a seller and a product, meeting at the gap. Magazine pacing, tilted crops, navy-to-coral grade, a horizontal gallery of real stories, and a typographic map of Lebanon that lights up city by city.

EditorialHumanLocalPhotography-ledCommunity first
Open live mockup ↗

Signature motion

  1. Load: the two photo planes slide together from opposite corners, the headline lines rise from behind a mask.
  2. Horizontal story rail driven by vertical scroll; cards rotate to level at centre; images distort slightly on hover.
  3. The "chaos to order" pin: notes fly into the phone, one order pops out.
  4. City dots ping in sequence as the map enters; a ticker of merchant names runs under the hero.

Best if

Axisel wants to win on trust and belonging rather than on feature lists. Nobody in the category shows real Lebanese merchants at this scale. It also gives the community pillar (a stated brand value) a home on the site.

Watch out for

  • Requires a real photoshoot before launch: six to ten merchants, hard light, tilted crops. Without it the concept collapses into stock, which the guide forbids.
  • Heaviest on images; needs an aggressive image pipeline and a strict performance budget.
  • Product proof is lighter; pair it with a solid Platform page.
Concept C

One System

The product is the hero. An exploded stack of five glass surfaces (storefront, catalog, orders, campaigns, analytics) floats at 23.5° over Ink Navy and assembles into one system as you scroll, while a live order feed ticks in from Instagram. Gold is the signal, coral is "now." A bone-coloured break keeps it from becoming another dark page.

Product-immersiveNavy-firstLive dataSafest evolutionLinear-grade polish
Open live mockup ↗

Signature motion

  1. Load: layers explode upward one by one; blooms breathe behind them; the first live order arrives.
  2. Scroll: the stack collapses into a single surface (pin + scrub); numbers count; stock updates when an order lands.
  3. Cursor parallax tilts the stack; each surface has a real hover state.
  4. Grain over the navy, gradient blooms that drift slowly, never a static flat black.

Best if

The client wants the continuity of a dark, product-forward site (what exists today, done properly) and the strongest demonstration of the software itself. Best for a buyer who needs to see orders, stock, and campaigns before they believe the promise.

Watch out for

  • It is the most common shape in the category (Linear, Vercel, Stripe). The brand angle, serif, and warmth are what keep it from reading as a template.
  • The UI mocks must match the real admin. Fake screens erode trust fast.
  • Least community-forward; needs the merchant and event content elsewhere.
Concept D · A 80% + B 20%

Together on Axis

Everything Concept A is, with Concept B's people inside it. The axis geometry and physics stay untouched: bone ground, the giant mark, the hairline sweep, the planes that part on scroll. What B adds is the merchants, photographed in tilted, graded crops and cut into the mark's own plane shapes, so every merchant story is literally a mark assembling: the person on one plane, the product on the other, meeting at the gap.

From B (20%)

  • Merchant names ticker under the hero.
  • Merchant chips on the hero proof line.
  • One merchant card inside the opening.
  • The Merchants section: story marks made of two photo planes each, with quotes.
  • Merchant avatar in the dashboard; the 1,200+ stat; "Merchants" in the navigation.

Signature motion and watch-outs

  • Each story's two photo planes slide in from opposite corners and lock into the mark as the section enters: B's hero animation, at card scale.
  • Hovering a story mark opens the gap slightly to reveal the quote.
  • Keep photography at this dose. If photos spread to every section it becomes B, and the geometry stops reading.
  • Launches with three merchants and grows; a proper shoot can come after launch.

Direction: Concept D.

It keeps everything the client responded to in A, the 23.5° geometry and the physics, and folds in B's warmth exactly where the brand's Community value needs a home. The product proof from A's "Build for real" panel stays. The one discipline to hold during the build is the photo dose: merchants appear in four places and nowhere else. Next step is the design spec.

04 · The stack

Astro 7 is the right call. Here is why, and what goes with it.

This is a content site with a few intensely animated islands, which is exactly the shape Astro is built for. Astro 7 shipped on 22 June 2026 (Rust compiler, Vite 8 with Rolldown, stable route caching), and needs Node 22 or newer.

Framework

Astro 7

Zero JavaScript by default, so the pages stay fast on Lebanese mobile networks; islands only where motion lives. Content collections for templates, merchant stories, and events. Built-in image service, view transitions for the page-to-page choreography, i18n routing ready for an Arabic version. Static output deployable to Vercel, Netlify, or Cloudflare unchanged.

Motion

GSAP 3 + Lenis

GSAP with ScrollTrigger, SplitText, and Flip (all free since 2025) for pinning, scrubbing, and text choreography; Lenis for smooth scroll. Everything honours prefers-reduced-motion and degrades to a static, readable page.

3D, only where it earns it

Three.js or OGL

Concept A's hero mark and Concept C's stack are the only places that justify WebGL. OGL is a fraction of Three's size; either loads as a lazy island with a static fallback. Concept B needs no WebGL at all.

Content and delivery

Markdown / MDX, Vercel or Cloudflare

Copy lives in typed content collections so the client can edit without touching layout. A headless CMS can be added later without a rewrite. Performance budget: Lighthouse 95+ on mobile, first contentful paint under 1.5 s on a mid-range phone.

Why not Next.js again: the site is not an application, and the current build already shows the cost (client-only pricing, JavaScript for everything). SvelteKit or Nuxt would work, but neither beats Astro's default of shipping no JavaScript for the 90 percent of the page that is text and images.

05 · Next steps
  1. Confirm Concept D. Open the live mockup; it animates on load, the story marks assemble on scroll, and the cards respond to hover.
  2. Design spec. I write the full site design: pages, sections, copy direction, motion system, components, and the content the client needs to supply.
  3. Implementation plan and build in Astro 7, page by page, with the homepage first so the client sees the concept in motion early.
  4. Content. Real merchant names and numbers, the pricing table, template library, and, for B, the photoshoot brief.
